headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create dangerous default interaction between Cline and Kestra; compliance and cascading-error risks are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP, while Kestra reads/writes files and can ingest workflow inputs. That creates a plausible shared-file bridge where attacker-controlled content from one can influence the other. The pathway is not proven by evidence, so I avoid high, but the default shared filesystem makes injection realistic.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or storage path
IF Kestra consumes files produced by Cline without content validation
IF Cline loads untrusted file content into prompts or tool instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces and storage paths
Disable MCP servers that read shared files
Add content provenance tags before file handoff
Require manual review of any file-derived instructions
requires-engineering: add sandboxed, read-only handoff directories

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; Kestra handles logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and notifications. If they share a workspace or pipeline, sensitive data can flow from Cline into Kestra outputs or external services. The blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance breach, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Cline is given secrets, screenshots, or proprietary code in the same workspace Kestra can access
IF Kestra forwards workflow data to Slack, email, cloud, or other APIs
IF shared files are mounted into both agents without redaction
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared folders
Restrict Kestra connectors to non-sensitive destinations
Turn off Cline network egress for sensitive sessions
Use separate service accounts and storage buckets
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read and write filesystems, and Cline also modifies git state. With shared filesystem-based concurrency and no documented locking between them, concurrent writes can corrupt worktrees, workflows, or generated artifacts. Because the overlap is broad and defaults are unsafe, high fits better than medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or output directory
IF Kestra tasks and Cline sessions run concurrently
IF no external lock or lease mechanism serializes writes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Use git locks or a single committer
Make Kestra outputs append-only where possible
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived findings, and file edits; Kestra can trigger downstream tasks, notifications, and cloud actions. If Kestra treats Cline output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious suggestion can cascade into emails, deployments, or data moves. The pair therefore has a default path from generated content to action-taking authority.
conditions: IF Kestra ingests Cline-produced files or text as workflow inputs
IF downstream tasks act on those inputs without verification
IF notifications or cloud actions are enabled in the workflow
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before execution
Validate Cline outputs against schemas
Limit Kestra to dry-run mode for generated artifacts
Require checksum or signature checks on handoffs
requires-engineering: add policy gates before action tasks

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots, while Kestra processes logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications. If regulated or EU personal data enters the shared workflow, Kestra's broad API integrations and storage surfaces can move it across services or regions without a documented DPA/residency control. That creates a compliance-breach pathway in default use.
conditions: IF EU personal data, PHI, or other regulated data is processed by both agents
IF Kestra routes that data to third-party APIs or cloud services
IF retention or residency settings are not explicitly constrained
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to either agent
Disable nonessential external connectors
Set explicit retention limits in Kestra
Keep regulated data out of Cline screenshots and workspaces
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA controls per workflow
